newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's top restaurants must cut prices - study.
newsitem.headline: France's top restaurants must cut prices - study.

text.p: France's gourmet restaurants must tone down their snobbish image and cut prices if they do not wish to see their fortunes collapse like a failed souffle, according to an industry study released on Thursday.

Luxury restaurants "must do all they can to make themselves more accessible, by offering their services at more justifiable and more affordable prices and in a more relaxing atmosphere", said the study by the Paris Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

While 98 percent of French people believe fine cooking to be a basic element of their heritage, 70 percent feel it is a pleasure reserved for only a small number of their fellow citizens, an IPSOS opinion poll conducted for the chamber said.
More than two-thirds of those questioned said the main reason they would not go to a gourmet restaurant was the high prices. Nearly half said they could not imagine spending so much money for a meal.

Defining a gourmet restaurant as one in which the average bill was 200 francs ($40) or more including tax, tip and drinks, the chamber found 6,250 in France with total annual turnover of 30 billion francs ($6 billion). Together they serve 60 million meals a year.
The luxury sector makes up 8.6 percent of all restaurants in France but dishes up two percent of all restaurant meals and accounts for 15 percent of total restaurant turnover.
France's top restaurants have been hard hit by slow economic growth and soaring costs in recent years.
Many of the best-known gourmet restaurants have had to open up lower-cost bistros next door to keep customers coming.
The Pierre Gagnaire Restaurant in the central town of Saint-Etienne became the first three-star restaurant in history to have to close its doors after declaring bankruptcy.
